docs.task: How the `ostra stop` command stops a session offline, and how the CLI is defined.

asks: Explain how `ostra stop` stops a session offline
Explain how the CLI is defined

data_flow.step: User runs `ostra stop <session-id>`. `Cli::parse()` yields `Command::Stop { session }`. Before parsing, `main` handles the hidden `sandbox-init` argument and scrubs the startup env.
`main` calls `ostra_server::app::stop_offline(&session)` synchronously (no `block_on`) and prints `Stopped {session}; {n} running executions were cancelled.`

`stop_offline` bails with a message pointing to the board or `POST /api/sessions/{session}/stop` when `server_running()` is true. `server_running` reads `<data dir>/server.json`, takes `pid`, and checks the process is alive (`kill(pid, 0)`, EPERM counts as alive). A missing or unparsable file or dead pid means not running.

`open_registry()` opens the registry db (creating the data dir, setting 0600 on the db and its -wal/-shm files on unix). `registry.list_workspaces()` is iterated; for each workspace, `paths::workspace_db(&w.root)` is checked for existence and opened with `WorkspaceDb::open`. The first workspace whose `db.get_session(&id)` is `Some` wins. If none, error `No registered workspace has a session {session}.`

`stop_session_offline(&db, &id)` folds the events. Errors: `NotFound` when the session has no events, `Invalid("This session has already ended.")` when `is_terminal()` (completed or failed). It does not check `paused`.

For each running execution (no result in fold): build `ExecutionResult` Cancelled with error `STOPPED_BY_USER`, copy `usage` and `native_session_id` from `db.get_execution`, call `db.finish_execution` (error ignored), append `ExecutionFinished`.
Append `SessionFailed { error: STOPPED_BY_USER }`, then `db.update_session` sets status Failed, lane Done, and stage_label `Stopped: Stopped by the user.`. Returns the count of cancelled executions.

On the next server start, `Engine::recover` folds each session. Because the folded state has `failed` set, `is_terminal()` is true and `ensure_driver` is not called, so the session is not driven again. Executions already finished are not marked Interrupted by `recover`.

patterns.description: `Cli` derives `Parser` with `command: Option<Command>` and flattened `ServeArgs`, so a bare `ostra` runs the server (`None => serve(cli.serve)`) and `ostra serve` runs it too. Each subcommand is a `Command` variant whose doc comment is its `--help` text. `Stop` takes one positional `session: String`. `main` is synchronous, builds a multi-thread tokio runtime, and offline commands (Stop, Config, Sessions, Signout, Url) run without `block_on`, while Hook, McpStdio and Serve use the runtime.
patterns.name: clap derive CLI with optional subcommand and flattened serve args

patterns.description: Every state change is an event (CLAUDE.md pattern 1), and the offline path appends them with `WorkspaceDb::append_event` instead of `Inner::append`, so nothing is folded in memory or broadcast, because no engine is running. The session state is rebuilt from `db.events` with `SessionState::fold`. Offline stop writes, per running execution, `finish_execution` plus an `ExecutionFinished` event with status Cancelled, then one `SessionFailed` event with `STOPPED_BY_USER`, then updates the materialized session row (status Failed, lane Done, stage_label).
patterns.name: Offline stop mirrors the online stop and recovery by appending events directly to the db

document.problem: `ostra stop <session>` ends a session while no server process holds it, so the next server start does not recover the session and re-run its interrupted executions. It bypasses the Engine and writes to the workspace SQLite database directly. The CLI is a single clap derive definition in the `ostra` binary crate.

submit.findings_summary: The CLI is one clap derive definition in crates/ostra-server/src/main.rs: `Cli` has an optional `Command` and flattened `ServeArgs`, and `Stop { session }` is one variant. `main` calls `app::stop_offline`, which refuses if `server.json`'s pid is alive (`auth::server_running`). Otherwise it scans registered workspaces for the one whose db holds the session and calls `runner::stop_session_offline`. That function folds the events and rejects ended sessions. It cancels each running execution, keeping its usage, appends `SessionFailed` with "Stopped by the user.", and updates the session row to Failed/Done. On the next start `Engine::recover` sees a terminal session and does not drive it. A test in crates/ostra-engine/tests/recover.rs and docs/architecture/server.md cover this.

docs.task: How the workspace db lists sessions and their statuses.

asks: Explain how the workspace db lists sessions.
Explain how the workspace db represents and returns session statuses.

data_flow.step: An event is appended for a session (user action, execution result, gate answer). `Inner::append` stores it with `db.append_event`, which also touches `sessions.updated_at` in the same transaction.
The event is folded into the in-memory `SessionState`, and `view::summary` derives the `SessionSummary`, including `SessionStatus`.

The derived status, lane, stage label, and other fields are written to the `sessions` row with `WorkspaceDb::update_session` (one UPDATE per set column, inside a transaction). The row is re-read with `get`, then `EngineNotice::SessionUpdated` is broadcast.

A reader calls `WorkspaceDb::list_sessions`. It locks the connection, reads the workspace id from `meta`, and runs `SELECT {COLS} FROM sessions ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC`. `COLS` includes the `open_gates` subquery over `gates`.
Each row becomes a `SessionSummary` through `session()`, where `status` is parsed from the stored string with `r.variant("status")`, and `kind` and `projects` are parsed from JSON.

The caller uses the full list: the REST handler returns it as JSON; `WorkspaceRt::busy`, `project_busy`, `project_views`, `list_workspaces`, `git::session_in`, and `artifacts::blocked` filter by status; `Engine::recover` loads every session at server start.

Stopping: `Engine::stop_session` appends `SessionFailed { error: STOPPED_BY_USER }`, which the fold turns into status `Failed` on the row, then cancels each running execution's token and denies open permission gates. The offline path `stop_session_offline` cancels running executions in the db, appends events, and sets status `Failed` and lane `Done` directly.

patterns.description: The `sessions` table is a projection. `Inner::append` appends the event, applies it to the in-memory `SessionState`, computes `view::summary`, and writes status, lane, stage label, projects, yolo, cost, category, and title back with `update_session`. Errors from that write are ignored (`let _ =`). The list therefore returns what the last event produced, not a live recomputation. `SessionStatus` is chosen in `view::summary` in this order: completed, failed, paused, waiting (open gates and no running execution), otherwise running. `Stalled` is declared in the enum but no code in `crates` assigns it.

patterns.description: The db exposes no status filter. Every caller that needs live sessions calls `list_sessions()` and matches on `Running | Waiting | Paused` (some add `Stalled`; the sweep uses `Completed | Failed`). The set of live statuses is repeated at each site rather than named once.

document.problem: The workspace db keeps one row per session in a materialized `sessions` table and returns the whole table as `Vec<SessionSummary>`, newest first, with no filtering. Callers that need only live sessions fetch every row and filter on `status` in Rust. The status column is a projection of the event-sourced session state that the engine rewrites on every appended event, so the column is only as fresh as the last event.

submit.findings_summary: WorkspaceDb::list_sessions runs `SELECT ... FROM sessions ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC` with no filter. It computes `open_gates` with a subquery over `gates` and returns `Vec<SessionSummary>`. The `sessions.status` column holds a snake_case `SessionStatus` string. The engine rewrites it on every appended event: `view::summary` derives it from the fold (completed, failed, paused, waiting, else running), and `Inner::append` writes it with `update_session`. `Stalled` is declared but never assigned. Callers such as `WorkspaceRt::busy`, `project_busy`, `project_views`, `list_workspaces`, `git::session_in`, and `artifacts::blocked` fetch all rows and filter on Running, Waiting, and Paused in Rust. Stopping is per session only (`Engine::stop_session`, which appends `SessionFailed`, and `stop_session_offline`). No route stops every session in a workspace.
